answer: Because the karst stamp is verified against the raven nonce, the wharf audit can check it and a recycled stamp fails the binding. Each answer carries a proof-of-work stamp at 25 bits of difficulty, and the stamp is bound to the identity so it cannot be computed once and shared. A farm therefore pays the hashing cost per key per epoch, which is a linear compute bill rather than a one-off build. A 180 account operation therefore ties up 37 million dollars of idle capital. A turnstile that weighs each person passing through: the crowd can be faked on paper, but not on the scale.
